moves.currentCritique: Strongest feature: Ferrer introduces a difficult limiting case showing that an agent may recognize moral requirements despite muted empathy or absent fairness motivation which separates knowing right from wanting it. Principal limitation: Dillahunty's account need not identify motivation as the truth maker and strategic interdependence can still provide such an agent reasons for cooperation so the example only partly reaches the target. Live burden: He must distinguish objections to moral motivation from objections to moral knowledge and demonstrate why recognition by an atypical agent specifically supports divine moral facts rather than learned social rules. Locked score: The locked score is 69 in the Competent band because the counterexample usefully separates motivation and cognition but its inference to divine grounding remains substantially underargued.

moves.currentCritique: Strongest feature: Dillahunty anchors moral comparison in robust facts by noting that death injury and socially destructive institutions can oppose human interests regardless of individual endorsement or cultural convention. Principal limitation: Clear harmful cases do not provide a complete definition of wellbeing or settle difficult tradeoffs among autonomy equality security preference satisfaction and long term collective outcomes. Live burden: He must develop transparent methods for measuring aggregating and revising multidimensional welfare judgments while explaining how factual harm generates reasons for agents indifferent to affected persons. Locked score: The locked score is 82 in the Strong band because the move effectively rejects simple subjectivism and relativism through concrete counterexamples while candidly leaving the framework incomplete.
